sections.bodyEn: Lume – and even more lume At its base lies an all-new dial, printed with multiple layers of Super-LumiNova® and arranged in a shimmering sunray pattern. On the Lumière Neon, the lower two sectors glow blue, while the upper area is a vivid green. With the Nova, the sunray-patterned dial has been printed with Super-LumiNova® White X1 for maximum impact.
Sunray-patterned dial printed with Super-LumiNova® for after-dark illumination.
Sunray-patterned dial printed with Super-LumiNova® for after-dark illumination.
A Globolight® ring and tipped hands for nocturnal accuracy
‘Songbird’ striking hammer hits the steel spring to achieve the ‘beautiful singing’ of the D note
The 41mm Light-catcher™ case is forged from Grade 5 titanium to amplify the sound of the chime

Redesigned and slimmer Light-catcher™ case. NEW Sellita SW200-2 Power+ automatic movement with 65-hour power reserve. NEW conical crown – without guards. Fully polished bezel. Sapphire ‘exhibition’ caseback. NEW polished lacquer dial. Slimmer polished hands. Simpler seconds hand – with non-Trident counterbalance. Diamond-polished and tapered indexes – filled with lume. NEW in-house-designed rotor with skeletonised arm. Raised, applied date window at 6 o’clock. ‘Sealander’ logotype on the dial for the first time. The debut of iLink™, a system that enables tool-free link adjustment on Bader and Consort™ bracelets. Also available on sporty rubber strap with Bader buckle. Available in the NEW warmer White, NEW Pistachio, NEW Pink, Sky Blue plus Black – in both 36mm and 39mm.

Finishing the movement is a new refined, skeletonised rotor: sandblasted beneath, with raised Christopher Ward text and a debossed twin-flags logo. Linear brushing across the upper surfaces contrasts with concentric circular brushing on the rotor weight – considered detailing, executed with precision.
Slimmer 10.9mm Light-catcher™ case
New conical crown without crown guards
Diamond-polished, 4 faceted, tapered indexes
Ingenious new iLink™ system
Linear and circular brushed skeletonised rotor arm

NEW polished lacquer dial. NEW slimmer, four-faceted polished hands. Simpler seconds hand – with non-Trident counterbalance. Diamond-polished and tapered indexes – filled with lume. Bolder, fully painted GMT hand. Sellita SW330-2 movement with 56-hour power reserve. NEW in-house-designed rotor with skeletonised arm. Reproportioned, larger bezel at a shallower angle for increased legibility. ‘Sealander’ logotype on the dial for the first time. NEW 42mm size. The debut of iLink™, a system that enables tool-free link adjustment on Bader and Consort™ bracelets. Also available on sporty rubber strap with Bader buckle. Available in the NEW warmer White, NEW Pistachio, NEW Pink, Sky Blue plus Black.

Finishing the movement is a new refined, skeletonised rotor: sandblasted beneath, with raised Christopher Ward text and a debossed twin-flags logo. Linear brushing across the upper surfaces contrasts with concentric circular brushing on the rotor weight – considered detailing, executed with precision.
Re-proportioned bezel and slimmer Light-catcher™ case

Sellita SW300-1 COSC Automatic Launched in 2008, Sellita’s 25-jewel SW300-1 automatic movement is one of the most respected calibres in Swiss watchmaking. At 25.6mm in diameter and with a height of 3.6 mm (one millimetre less than the SW200-1), it has a frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour (4 Hz) and boasts a power reserve of 56 hours. Seen as an alternative to ETA’s 2892-A2 calibre, the SW300-1 can be customised with various complications, including date, moonphase, and GMT functions.
Crunchy, sugar-crystal dial in six high-calorie shades.
Exhibition caseback with sweet Pic ’n’ Mix printing.
Thirty-six millimetre, Grade 2 titanium case finished three ways.
Each watch is packaged with a striped Pic ’n’ Mix paper bag.

Sellita SW300 Automatic Powering the C60 Sapphire Edge is Sellita’s 25-jewel SW300 automatic movement, which boasts a power reserve of 56 hours. At 25.6mm in diameter and with a height of 3.6mm – one millimetre less than the SW200-1 – its thinner profile helped us reduce the case thickness and increase the watch’s wearability.
Sapphire The sapphire countdown bezel adds a refined sheen without compromising toughness. It’s engineered to provide the perfect ‘click’.
The sapphire countdown bezel adds a refined sheen without compromising toughness. It’s engineered to provide the perfect ‘click’.
Sellita’s 25-jewel SW300 automatic movement isn’t just accurate, but also provides a power reserve of 56 hours.
From the lume of the Aquaflex rubber strap to the Super-LumiNova-filled handset and indexes, the Edge places luminosity front and centre.

Housing it all is a newly developed 40.5mm Light-catcher™ case, fitted with box-domed sapphire crystals front and back. The case’s carefully balanced proportions ensure the watch sits comfortably on the wrist, while alternating brushed and polished surfaces emphasise the signature Light-catcher™ geometry. Completing the design is a newly refined Bader bracelet with polished bevels on each link, a graceful taper, and a micro-adjust clasp for travelling comfort. Or a new FKM rubber strap – snuggly integrated at the lug with a textured upper and deployant Bader buckle.
Conceived by technical director Frank Stelzer, it’s built on the foundations of Calibre CW-001 – formerly ‘Calibre SH21’ – the five-day, twin-barrelled movement we launched in 2014.

The first True GMT calibre from a British brand, CW-002 is COSC-certified and joins the small, elite circle of GMT movements. Built on CW-001, it integrates a new GMT mechanism without increasing movement height.
40.5mm Light-catcher™ case with box-domed sapphire crystals front and back, alternating brushed and polished surfaces, and balanced proportions for everyday comfort.
Diamond-polished hour, minute, and small seconds hands, all filled with Super-LumiNova® for low-light legibility; GMT hand and power-reserve indicator lacquered for contrast.

Partially open and deliberately layered, the dial prioritises local time and home time while recessing secondary indicators. Small seconds, power reserve, date, and exposed GMT bridge add depth and utility.
Rhodium-plated movement with circular Côtes de Genève, visible twin barrels and balance wheel, and a tungsten rotor with sunray-polished and sandblasted surfaces.
Applied markers, polished and faceted, filled with Super-LumiNova® for clear visibility in all conditions.

Depth by design The C1 Jump Hour Mk V has a dramatically complex four tier dial construction. At the centre sits a three-dimensional inner piece stamped with 27 concentric circles. A polished, applied circular-brushed metal ring rises above, and beyond this, a sapphire ring printed with minute markers. A sapphire minute hand with a unique stepped-design - a first for Christopher Ward. Completed by a multi-Super-LumiNova® layered undercoat, for an ethereal, cool blue glow in low light.
Mastery of sapphire – heavily box-domed crystal, and unique design sapphire minute hand
Mastery of sapphire – heavily box-domed crystal, and unique design sapphire minute hand
The four-tier dial creates extraordinary visual depth by day, and by night
Dial ring and minute hand are undercoated with multiple layers of Super-LumiNova®
Detailed caseback denoting the 12-hour stops of the jump hour wheel and the minutes between
Low-light legibility in a truly original way our sapphire dial ring allows every concealed hour to charge, offering all-night time-telling

The Bel Canto Classic sits alongside the original, but brings something more complex, more traditional – more, well, classic. The box sapphire crystal delivers mid-century Italian charm, while the Roman numerals on the time-telling dial add the elegance of something that's never needed to shout. If the original Bel Canto was made for the awards ceremony, the Classic makes its mark at the invite-only aperitivo.

sections.titleEn: FS01: the mechanism behind the music

sections.bodyEn: An extrapolation of our JJ01 ‘jumping hour’ module, Calibre FS01 creates a D-note chime thanks to a U-shaped gong that doubles back on itself around the rim of the face, and a bird-shaped hammer mechanism, where the beak indicates whether the complication is on or off, and the tail strikes to make the sound.

Advanced ‘femto’ lasers render Bel Canto Classic's guilloché finish in three dimensions – a technique that creates greater detail and intricacy than traditional punched guilloché ever could. In Negroni, that shimmering effect becomes something else entirely. Deep scarlet in stillness. Warm amber on the move. The colour of Campari held up to the last light of the evening.

With much of the face given up to key mechanical parts in a glorious open-worked style, Bel Canto relies for its time-telling on a smaller subdial that ‘floats’ over the platine, the base-layer disc a watch like this has in place of a traditional dial. It all gives a fascinating feeling of depth, while the elegant simplicity of Roman numerals and a new, restrained handset emphasise the Classic’s old-school refinement.

Christopher Ward’s famous Light-catcher™ case has proved to be one of our most crucial, versatile signatures, and with Bel Canto it’s had a subtle makeover to help it best reverberate with sound. The first ever CW case to be made from Grade 5 titanium – less dense than steel, so it amplifies the chime – it’s been optimised inside and out to produce the most pleasing possible chime.

Open-worked watches like Bel Canto feature fascinating multi-layered architecture, so some components exist below the coloured platine, while others are displayed proudly above it – not least the vital hammer, the gong, and the bridges that support them. All are, of course, exquisitely polished by some of Switzerland’s finest finishers.

sections.titleEn: The crystal that earns its place
sections.bodyEn: A box sapphire crystal, unique to the Bel Canto’s Classic, reproduces much of the charming look and feel of vintage acrylic crystals, while retaining all the scratch-resistance of sapphire. It even visually slims the watch slightly, too: win-win (and, indeed, win).

Calibre CW-001 Our first-ever in-house movement, and an immensely stable COSC-certified calibre with a remarkable 120-hour power reserve, achieved through twin mainspring barrels. It's as handsome as it is high performance. Over a decade old, the CW-001 continues to be a reliable and much-loved calibre and proof that strength and beauty aren't mutually exclusive.
The multi-angled bridgework is made with the Elara NS CNC milling machine.
The multi-angled bridgework is made with the Elara NS CNC milling machine.
Domed sapphire crystals let you view every shining surface of CW-001.
Lume-filled rhodium minute ring and handset deliver luminosity after dark.
The bracelet’s butterfly clasp has an adjustment mechanism – a first in The Twelve series – letting you change the length by up to 1.5mm per side - 3mm total.
The watch’s matte-black DLC coating whispers its presence.
CW-001 delivers chronometer accuracy with a five-day power reserve.

As with previous CW ‘ombré’ watches, the lacquered deep-brown dial gradually changes from light to dark toward the edge – without sacrificing legibility. The lume-filled handset delivers clarity and precision, while the ‘5N gold’ indexes – also filled with Super-LumiNova® – boast diamond-polished facets that catch the light. The date wheel at 6 o’clock is colour-matched to the dial, while the applied twin-flags logo – also in 5N gold – adds balance and depth.

Lacquered, shaded, perfected Each dial is spun at high speed during the application of paint – a process which takes the shade from light to dark as you move away from the centre. Layers of lacquer are then applied to increase its lustre.

Each dial is spun at high speed during the application of paint – a process which takes the shade from light to dark as you move away from the centre. Layers of lacquer are then applied to increase its lustre.
If you like to see elite Swiss watchmaking up close, the chronometer-certified Sellita SW200 automatic movement, accurate to -4/+6 seconds per day, can be enjoyed through the clear caseback.
Both the 42mm and 44mm bronze Light-catcher™ case has been designed to stand out, but thanks to its sculpted form, will sit close to your wrist. It’ll also develop a unique patina over time.
Engineered for pro-diving use, the unidirectional 120-click bezel is crafted from non-scratch ceramic, deep-filled with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1 for visibility in low light.

sections.titleEn: A case to fall in love with
sections.bodyEn: Both CW’s twin-flags logo, which represents the company’s English and Swiss arms, and the ‘5N gold’ indexes, have been applied to the dial – adding depth and balance.

Whichever model you choose, the perfectly chamfered hour indexes have been filled with even more Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1, while the twin-flags logo is applied – and carries a subtle brushed finish. The lume-filled handset makes telling the time a dream, while the fourth brightly-coloured GMT hand – also filled with lume – lets you monitor another time zone with accuracy, day or night.

Greenwich mean time The ‘GMT’ stands for Greenwich Mean Time – mean solar time at the Prime Meridian in Greenwich, London. It serves as a global time standard, often used to coordinate time across different regions – hence its use in aviation, and following this, as a horological complication.

The ‘GMT’ stands for Greenwich Mean Time – mean solar time at the Prime Meridian in Greenwich, London. It serves as a global time standard, often used to coordinate time across different regions – hence its use in aviation, and following this, as a horological complication.
Sellita’s 25-jewel GMT calibre lets you monitor any of the world’s time zones, by bringing the GMT hand together with the 24-hour bezel. It also delivers a power reserve of up to 56 hours.

The bi-directional ceramic bezel has been split into two colours to separate ‘night’ and ‘day’ sections on the 24-hour clock – with luminous numerals on the ‘day’ half. Using the bezel with the GMT hand allows you to monitor up to three time zones.
Whether you choose the black or white model, the highly polished surface provides a perfect background for the handset, and a home for the date window and applied logo.
If you’re a lume-lover – guilty! – then the larger indexes and handset are deep-filled with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1 for timekeeping in the dark.

Everything about the C60 Trident Pro 300 is made for daily wear: smart enough for the office, rugged enough to accompany you on the deepest of dives. Its unidirectional bezel boasts a rotating outer section with coloured ceramic insert, and a fixed steel inner ring, with minute increments all the way around.

“Christopher Ward’s reputation has skyrocketed because of its refusal to abide by the insane markup status quo of other high-end watchmakers. It also has the internet to thank, since the brand’s popularity on watch forums has helped it secure itself as a cult favorite as well.” – Ethan Brehm, Writer
The Light-catcher™ case – available in 38, 40, 42 and 44mm sizes – is waterproof to 300m, which has enabled our engineers to reduce its thickness by up to 1.9mm.
Our twin-flags logo, which represents CW’s joint centres of England and Switzerland, is at 12 o’clock, while balance is provided by the date window, with self-coloured date disc, at 6.

The redesigned bracelet, crafted in marine-grade stainless steel, boasts an increased taper – 16.5mm at the clasp – and an improved micro-adjustment mechanism. Plus, it now boasts screw links rather than pins.
If you like to see Swiss horology in the metal, the highly-finished Sellita SW200-1 automatic movement can be viewed through the transparent crystal case back.

Thanks to the genius of Calibre JJ04, our in-house modular movement, the moon is linked to the hour hand and is in constant motion, with the phases of the moon represented in a single smooth movement. If the watch is kept wound, JJ04 delivers accuracy for 128 years. And you can see the magic of mechanical watchmaking by turning the piece over and gazing through the sapphire case back at the movement.

Unlike most moonphase complications that transition once per day, JJ04 offers a more dynamic approach. Using the Sellita SW220 as a base, the date wheel, along with its spring-loading assembly, have been stripped out and replaced by four further wheels to drive the moon disc, with two more required for the setting mechanism.

The dial is made from aventurine – a translucent glass invented on the island of Murano, Venice – infused with reflective flakes of copper oxide that resemble the night sky. The radically unadorned dial carries no markings apart from the words ‘Swiss Made’ at 6 o’clock, so you can experience both the beauty of the oversized moon, and the shimmer of aventurine as it plays with the light.

The moonphase is powered by CW’s own modular movement, JJ04, which is able to follow the waxing (and waning) of the moon accurately for 128 years. This also allows the watch’s ‘moons’ to chart a continuous, uninterrupted journey across the dial.

If you like to get close to the magic of traditional watchmaking, you can view the movement through the exhibition back. Note the decorated rotor, which transfers energy to the mainspring and powers the watch.

Constructed in Globolight, a ceramic-Super-LumiNova mix which allows for intricate sculpting, the moon – or moons, there are two in constant rotation – is 25 percent bigger than any previous CW ‘moon’. The increased aperture lets you view even more ‘moon’ than ever before.

Slick, highly technical, supremely well-considered and innovative across the board, The C12 Loco is Christopher Ward at its most modern, most exciting, and most unexpected: a glittering, ever-moving, none-more-alive landmark watch to appeal to the child in each of us, yes, but to the technocrat too. As elite-level haute-horology made accessible to all, it’s one of the most explicit iterations of the Christopher Ward mission to date.

For all its intricate, whirring elegance, you never for one moment forget that The C12 Loco is a sports watch, with everything that implies: technical ability; a crisp, clean contemporary confidence. It’s nothing less than the spiritual child of Louis Cartier and Le Corbusier working in unlikely but delightful harmony…

The C12 Loco’s dial is a thing of beauty, with three vertically stacked circles from twelve to six, held by strong horizontal lines: bridges supporting the floating balance, small toothed escapement, and a just-off-centre step to accommodate the time-telling dial. There’s depth and detail everywhere—from visible gears in the trench beneath the hands to the ‘ski-jump’ drop-off, above which a vertical brushed finish contrasts with the lightly grained grené surface below. The white has different hands and grené throughout.

The C12 Loco’s brand new, custom-designed, free-sprung balance wheel and particularly fine 0.045mm hairspring (that’s less than the width of most human hairs) constantly oscillate before your eyes. Regulated by tiny screws (replacing traditional pins for extra precision), it oscillates at a frequency of 4Hz, which amounts to 28,800 vibrations (or beats) per hour.

From the large and incredibly clear time-telling dial at 12 o’clock – featuring generous amounts of lume on both hands and markers for maximum legibility – to the intricate, ever-moving floating balance just below it, The C12 Loco is a feast of just-so facets and endless delicate hand-polishing, creating a watch with such considered visual depth it’s a delight from every angle, (Hey, there’s over five hours of hand-finishing on the bridges alone.)

The C12 Loco takes Christopher Ward’s Twelve case and re-invents it, with a redesigned mid-case and a steeper downturn from case into bracelet, helping the watch contour more closely to the natural curve of the wrist. Best of all, you can see right into the heart of the watch through a gorgeous 3.35mm high glass box sapphire crystal at the front, and another to the rear.

Think ‘integrated bracelet sports watch’ and you think, of course, of finely-finished metal bands – and have we got a doozy for you. The much-admired Twelve bracelet is presented here in a new slimmed-down form which, with its 16mm taper, wears beautifully and suits the watch to a tee.

The C12 Loco’s rubber FKM straps come with our Bader Buckle and offer a striking alternative look, in a range of colours to match or – dramatic! – contrast with your dial. There’s no bad combination here, quite frankly, and the joy of Christopher Ward’s quick release technology making switching between them a breeze, why wouldn’t you consider buying a handful…?

The C12 Loco is Christopher Ward’s most ambitious watch to date – featuring a new in-house movement, the company’s highest-ever levels of finishing, and a dial design the watch world’s going to go mad for.

On the C60 Trident Lumière, the chamfered indexes are made entirely from Globolight XP©, as is the unmistakable ‘twin flags’ logo and most of the handset. In all, 17 specially-shaped blocks of Globolight XP© are used on the dial which contains five times the lume of any previous Trident (and which cost four times more to produce than a ‘regular’ dial). And because the dial comes in three extraordinary colour options – and whose ‘stippled grain’ surface adds extra texture – there’ll be a shade that’s right for you.
This chronometer version has been tested by the Contrôle Officiel Suisse des Chronomètres, in a number of positions and temperatures to ensure precision timekeeping.

The sculpted indexes, handset and ‘twin flags’ logo are all sculpted from blocks of Globolight XP© – a luminous ceramic created by Xenoprint, makers of Super-LumiNova® luminous paint. This means the luminosity of the Lumière is twice as bright as other Tridents.

The C60 Trident Lumière is constructed in Grade 2 titanium, which has the highest strength-to-weight ratio of any metal, which is why the watch head weighs only 53g. Yet thanks to titanium’s durability, Lumière is able to cope with the most challenging conditions – on land or at sea.

The 41mm brushed-and-polished Light-catcher™ case doesn’t just provide 300 metres of water-resistance, but is also our slimmest case ever with a height of 10.85mm. It’s been designed to sit flat and snug on the wrist, so you may forget you’re wearing it.

Ultra-precise timekeeping is provided by a COSC-certified version of Sellita’s SW300-1 movement, which also gives you a power reserve of 56 hours. The movement’s height of just 3.6mm is what makes Lumière’s slim silhouette possible.

Nothing demonstrates Lumière’s ambition better than its bracelet. Crafted in Grade 2 titanium, some facets are polished, others not, and the edges are beautifully chamfered. It boasts a taper to 16mm, and has a micro-adjustment mechanism – with a button marked ‘push’ – that lets you adjust the size by 6mm.

The helium release valve – integrated into the 41mm case – is activated during deep dives when the differential between the inside and outside pressure reaches a critical point, preventing the watch from cracking at depth.
Crafted from Grade 2 titanium and featuring an advanced luminous ceramic, the C60 Trident Lumière is the luxury diving watch that shines brighter.

The Extreme GMT also introduces our V-Strap – our first-ever quick-release sports strap designed for serious action. Built from military-grade Cordura® in a bold two-piece construction, it features our signature 4mm taper for optimal wrist fit, a logo-etched metal fastening, and industrial-strength Velcro® that lets you strip it off in seconds. Choose black or orange. Standard or XL. Ready when you are.

At just 4.1mm thick, the SW330-2 has 25 jewels and beats at a rate of 28,800 per hour with a power reserve of up to 56 hours. The central GMT hand can be set independently from the hour and seconds hands.
41mm brushed marine-grade, steel case with Light-catcher™ design. Combined with our first ever Sandblasted bezel.
The bright orange GMT hand – painted with Super-LumiNova® – enables you to monitor any time zone around the world.
18 separate pieces of Globolight® luminous ceramic deliver maximum lume when lights are low.
Deep-stamped steel backplate features a 20th century style globe motif.
A new rubberised anti-shock holder keeps the movement secure. In case of impact, the mount absorbs and distributes energy.
Our all-new V-Strap makes its debut on the Extreme. Military-grade Cordura® construction, quick-release Velcro® closing, logo-etched hardware.

The unidirectional bezel has been industrially sandblasted, providing a textured contrast to the super-visible raised numerals, while the triangle marker is filled with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1 to aid timing at depth. The product of extensive research, the bezel also delivers 120 clicks per rotation – providing you with tactile reassurance should you wish to use it as a diving aid.

The 26-jewel movement boasts a date wheel, a 4Hz frequency (equating to a smooth eight ticks per second) and a 38-hour power reserve. It also has an in-built anti-shock system to maintain accuracy when faced with any sudden jolts.
Each dial has been carefully lacquered, which takes the colour gradually from light to dark as you travel from the centre. Meanwhile, the date wheel is colour-matched to the dial.
Our twin-flags logo, which represents CW’s English/Swiss DNA, has been painstakingly applied to the dial by our in-house specialist.
If you like to see Swiss horology in the metal, the Sellita SW200-1 automatic movement, complete with CW-branded rotor, can be viewed through the transparent case back.
Love lume? The handset and indexes are filled with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1 for timekeeping at night – or in the depths of the ocean.
Engineered for professional diving use, the unidirectional 120-click bezel combines a heavily sandblasted surface with polished numerals – providing texture, contrast and clarity.

The watch’s chime comes courtesy of a steel spring which is placed around the edge of the dial. It’s been tuned so the sound is a delight for the ears while being loud enough to be heard from the wrist.
The time-telling subdial ‘floats’ over the sunray-finished Viola dial, giving the wearer a feeling of depth. The hands and indexes are filled with Super-LumiNova® for after-dark visibility.

The multi-layered architecture of the Bel Canto’s dial is enhanced by the exquisitely executed polishing of the hammer, spring and bridges – which together resemble a songbird. Crafted by hand (under microscope) by some of Switzerland’s finest artisans, finishing of this standard is usually the preserve of only the most exclusive and expensive brands.

Our Light-catcher™ case has had a subtle but sporty makeover. The first CW case made from Grade 5 titanium, the metal – which is less dense than steel – has been chosen for its ability to amplify sound. The internal architecture of the case has also been designed for the same reason.
By pressing the pusher at 4 o’clock on the side of the case, you can switch off the chime – something that’s shown in the movement of the red indicator on the dial.

sections.titleEn: A watch for the whole of your life
sections.bodyEn: The Twelve brings the pleasures of such pieces with none of the downsides. Fittingly, it’s home to some of Christopher Ward’s boldest design moves. It has a twelve-sided bezel – dodecagonal, no less – which gives a subtle scalloped look. It features a heavily textured three-dimensional dial, built of little moguls referencing the ‘pluses’ of the twin-flags logo. And it has a remarkable combination of intriguing surface finishes on case, bracelet and bezel.

Brace with impact The Twelve’s bracelet is built from single links to deliver a taper that goes from 25mm to 17mm, while the satinised finish comes courtesy of a water-grinding process. The bracelet closes with a butterfly clasp – fitted with a micro-adjustment mechanism. This allows the wearer to adjust the length by up to 1.5mm per side – and 3mm in total.

The Twelve’s bracelet is built from single links to deliver a taper that goes from 25mm to 17mm, while the satinised finish comes courtesy of a water-grinding process. The bracelet closes with a butterfly clasp – fitted with a micro-adjustment mechanism. This allows the wearer to adjust the length by up to 1.5mm per side – and 3mm in total.

sections.titleEn: We took our time, we thought differently, we built beautifully.
sections.bodyEn: Will Brackfield - designer

sections.titleEn: A dial to make you smile
sections.bodyEn: The Twelve’s three-dimensional pyramid pattern slyly references the twin-flags of the company logo and catches the light endlessly as your wrist moves. It comes in six great colours too.
An exhibition case back lets you admire the movement from the rear, while – in a playful tip of the hat to the Royal Oak – six large exposed screws hold down the 12-sided surround.
Even the hands and indices on the dial have been carefully reappraised, offering a riot of light-reflecting surfaces while using more understated and refined shapes than other Christopher Wards.

The stealth luxury represented by The Twelve requires every detail be given the utmost consideration. Look closely and you’ll see three different finishes – sandblasting, polishing and linear brushing – on the bezel alone.
Why the man behind Patek Philippe’s Nautilus and the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak is horology’s greatest designer.
Six years in the making. Endless experimentation. A pause until our team knew they could achieve their ambitions. Enjoy the story of our first integrated watch in 13 years.

Sellita SW200 COSC The C65 Dune Aeolian Bronze is gorgeous on the outside, but just as impressive beneath its ever-changing case, where you’ll find the strong, durable Swiss-made Sellita SW200 COSC Automatic movement, officially designated a ‘chronometer’ by the Contrôle Officiel Suisse des Chronomètres, and therefore amongst the most accurate mechanical movements around.

Strong but sleek, robust but elegant, bronze is especially alive, a metal that naturally develops a unique patina over time, giving your Dune Bronze an intriguingly muted, antique feel – which pairs gorgeously, of course, with its dial’s rich colours and precisely polished indices. Hey, as everyone knows: opposites attract.

Dune’s new face is brought to life by a striking three-dimensional horizontal wave pattern, built of two dozen or so stamped peaks and troughs – and, unique to the Bronze, combining a matte finish with a gradient effect, so the dial is lighter in the centre and darker at the edges, giving remarkable depth and distinctive character.

Though it speaks of historic seafaring and ancient weapons, this most bewitching of case metals also brings the Bronze a subtle luxury that’s unique amongst the Dunes. The toughest, grandest and most evocative, all at once? We’d say so.
Dune’s 38mm case is large enough to be easily read, yet small enough to neatly sidestep unwanted encounters with rocks and trees; even better, it looks great on any wrist.

Everywhere, you’ll find tiny improved details: these colours, those dials, and such small but telling design changes as the lack of a date window and the simplified seconds hand, without the Trident counterbalance. It all helps create a cleaner, less diluted, more harmonious design.

Inspired by the British Military’s quartz watches of the 1980s, the dial plays host to three subdials – controlled by pushers on the side of the case – which not only deliver a wealth of stopwatch options, but are dedicated to one of the Services through different coloured hands. And, in a first for a Military Collection, both the flat-polished numerals and logo have been applied for added depth.
Dial of delights The reverse panda dial boasts three subdials – with the hand of each one coloured to a particular Service: red for the Army; dark blue for the Navy; light blue for the RAF.
The reverse panda dial boasts three subdials – with the hand of each one coloured to a particular Service: red for the Army; dark blue for the Navy; light blue for the RAF.
The caseback features the heraldic crest of the Army, Navy and RAF. We’ve used the versions with the ‘Queen’s crown’ as a mark of respect to Queen Elizabeth II.
ETA G10.202 AD COSC quartz movement delivers not just incredible accuracy (+/- 10 seconds per year), but also a full range of stopwatch options.

sections.titleEn: A case you’ll love to wear
sections.bodyEn: The 39mm Light-catcher™ case isn’t just beautiful – check the way light bounces off its surfaces – but has also been designed to sit closer to your wrist.
Inspired by the design of the British Military’s quartz watches of the 1980s, the large numerals are applied and polished, as is CW’s ‘twin flags’ logo.

Sellita SW200 COSC Befitting a watch named for the British Army, the C65 Sandhurst is powered by extremely rugged and precise Swiss-made automatic movement - in this case, a chronometer-certified version of the Sellita SW200-1. Tested by the Controle Officiel Suisse des Chronometres, an institute responsible for ensuring the highest standards of horological excellence, the SW200-1 has been tested in a number of positions and temperatures to ensure precision timekeeping throughout.
“Each watch in the military collection sports some of the modern design touches from Christoper Ward.” – Thomas Calara

Inspired by the Smiths W10 field watch given to British soldiers in 1969, the improved C65 Sandhurst is a classic military timepiece. And like the W10, it’s been officially approved by the UK’s Ministry of Defence.
The C65 Sandhurst is the first Christopher Ward model authorised to carry the heraldic badge of the British Army. You’ll find it deep-stamped into the back.
The textured black dial is an exercise in legibility, while the use of our twin-flags logo both harks back to the no-name military watches of the past and CW’s latest design language.
Our 38mm Light-catcher™ case boasts brushed and polished surfaces which reflect light beautifully. Its ingenious design means it also sits on the wrist lower than you’d expect.

The Arabic numerals are printed with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1, while Old Radium Super-LumiNova® is applied to rectangular indexes located at each quarter-hour, along with five minute-positioned dots and a triangle at 12 o’clock.
Christopher Ward’s Military Collection gets its first upgrade since its launch in 2019 – with a set of stunning retro-style watches named after the Services’ world-famous training academies.

As with the original, the watch features a genuine super compressor mechanism – invented in the mid-1950s by case manufacturer Ervin Piquerez SA (EPSA) to allow divers to go deeper without their watch malfunctioning. An ultra-thin compression spring – just 300 microns wide – is placed around the perimeter of the case. When a diver descends, it uses water pressure to press the caseback against the O-ring gasket, increasing water-resistance.

Spring into the deep The ‘compression’ spring – the width of four human hairs – is key to the mechanics of the C65 Super Compressor Elite and enables the case to become more watertight as you descend. It’s placed within the compression ring and can be seen through the caseback.

The ‘compression’ spring – the width of four human hairs – is key to the mechanics of the C65 Super Compressor Elite and enables the case to become more watertight as you descend. It’s placed within the compression ring and can be seen through the caseback.

The interior countdown bezel – controlled by the cross-hatched crown at 2 o’clock – makes the watch sleeker than a regular dive timepiece. This allows the Supercompressor Elite to be worn under a shirt cuff with ease and makes it the perfect ‘dress-dive’ timepiece.

On the transparent caseback, you’ll find the ‘diving helmet’ emblem – the logo of the original super compressor manufacturer, Ervin Piquerez SA (EPSA) – stamped into a ‘coin’ that sits on top of the caseback.

Two crowns are on the side of the case. The first, at 2 o’clock, rotates the inner countdown bezel, while the lower crown, at 4 o’clock, controls the hands. Just like the crowns on the original super compressors, both have distinctive cross-hatching.
When it comes to wearability, we don’t cut corners. This 41mm cushioned Light-catcher™ case has brushed and polished surfaces and, thanks to its slim profile, easily slides under your cuff.

This is no ordinary dial. The decompression dial has been precision-printed so you can calculate stops at a glance. Meanwhile, the shades of orange and blue contrast beautifully without affecting legibility. Another retro touch is the authentic box-sapphire crystal.

On the C65 Super Compressor Elite, precision timekeeping is everything. That’s why the watch is powered by a chronometer version of the Sellita SW300 automatic calibre. This puts it in the top six percent of Swiss-made mechanical movements for accuracy.

Swiss perfection Unlike some moonphase complications that transition once per day, JJ04 offers a more dynamic approach. Using the Sellita SW220 as a base, the date wheel, along with its spring-loading assembly, have been stripped out and replaced by four further wheels to drive the moon disc, with two more required for the setting mechanism.

JJ04: perpetually brilliant The C1 Moonglow is powered by CW’s own modular movement, JJ04, which is able to follow the waxing (and waning) of the moon accurately for 128 years. This also allows the watch’s ‘moons’ to chart a continuous, uninterrupted journey across the dial.

The C1 Moonglow is powered by CW’s own modular movement, JJ04, which is able to follow the waxing (and waning) of the moon accurately for 128 years. This also allows the watch’s ‘moons’ to chart a continuous, uninterrupted journey across the dial.

The watch’s three-dimensional moons have increased amounts Grade X1 WL C1 Super-LumiNova® for an even better ‘moonglow’. While the precisely proportioned dial delivers more depth than found on the aventurine face of the C1 Moonphase.

The C1 Moonglow boasts a redesigned 40.5mm Light-catcher™ case, which makes it even more comfortable on the wrist, while the domed glass box crystal and polished facets on the lugs add a feeling of timeless luxury.
Replacing a conventional date window, a rotating ring – coated with Grade X1 WL C1 Super-LumiNova® – circles the dial and aligns with the current date on the outer-date ring.

And, like so many of our watches, the story of this 41mm diameter titanium version of The Twelve owes its creation more to impassioned conversation than any masterpiece of market positioning: on this occasion the lively conversation was between Will Brackfield, our senior designer, Jorg Bader Jnr, head of product development and me as we wandered through midtown New York on our way to visit the WatchTime show in New York on a drizzly Sunday morning. The first ‘X’ prototype, which we had recently been reviewing, was a joy to behold: the most extensive open-heart surgery of our 5 day chronometer movement had achieved a view, front and back, that took our collective breaths away. But on that walk to Gotham Hall on Broadway, we wondered aloud whether by pushing the aesthetic boundaries further by reconsidering finish of the bridges and by using two grades of titanium on the case, we could elevate it to an even higher plane, and make it even more special.

The multi-layered, multi-angled bridgework which supports the movement is only possible through the use of the Elara NS CNC milling machine, which uses a diamond cutter to achieve incredible accuracy. The work was undertaken by Paoluzzo, a maker of precision medical, aviation and horological parts.

Thanks to the domed sapphire crystals at both ends of the watch, you can view every part of SH21: from the twin barrels that deliver the famous five-day power reserve to the winding mechanism at 3 o’clock. The slim Super-LumiNova®-filled rhodium minute ring allows you to see more of the barrels and – another first – the escapement.
The dial is framed by a rhodium ring round the outside, with an applied luminous Globolight© wedge at 12 o’clock.

Grade 5 titanium – an alloy of titanium, aluminium and vanadium – is found on the bezel and case back. The material – which is harder than its Grade 2 counterpart – allows for improved mirror polishing, and offers a greater contrast to the satin-brushed finish of the rest of the case. A key design detail.

The Twelve X (Ti)’s bracelet is built from single links to deliver a taper that goes from 25mm to 17mm, while the satinised finish comes courtesy of a water-grinding process. The bracelet closes with a butterfly clasp – fitted with a micro-adjustment mechanism for the first time in The Twelve series. This allows the wearer to adjust the length by up to 1.5mm per side – and 3mm in total.

First created near Venice some 400 years ago, aventurine is a very special sort of glass, infused with reflective copper oxide flakes. With its entire dial made of this most charismatic of materials, the new Moonphase is able to perfectly imitate the star-speckled night sky. Since each piece of aventurine is different to any other, it makes every watch unique.

Built around surely the most romantic of all watch complications, our Moonphase echoes the waxing and waning of the moon with great accuracy – and for a mighty 128 years. For all this time, your watch’s own moons will chart a graceful unbroken journey across the dial’s star-splattered night-time sky.

We’re so keen to bring the Moonphase to more people, we moved heaven and earth to design a new C1 case at a more compact and accessible 37mm, while still allowing space inside for the moon phase complication.

With a spectacular dial made from aventurine – a special glass, invented on the island of Murano, that’s infused with reflective flakes of copper oxide – the Moonphase 37 represents the night sky with eerie accuracy. The beautifully stripped-back watch face carries nothing else (unless you count a tiny ‘Swiss Made’ legend) to ensure minimum distraction from your enjoyment of the lunar cycle.

Watching a great movement in action is one of the joys of traditional mechanical watchmaking, and with the Moonphase 37 you can do so effortlessly, thanks to a box sapphire exhibition back, upgraded from the flat glass of the 40.5mm version. The decorated rotor you’ll find here is the only place on the entire watch where the words ‘Christopher Ward’ appear.

We’re renowned for our full-blooded celebrations of the moon, so even on a more compact watch like the Moonphase 37, we’ve made certain to put our satellite front and centre, standing proud at 12 rather than hidden way at the bottom of the dial. Rarely has such an elegant piece been so glitteringly alive.

Built of Globolight©, a ceramic/Super-LumiNova mix that encourages the most intricate sculpting, our moon – or moons, for there are actually two in constant rotation – are 25 percent bigger than most. Even better, the over-sized nature of the aperture you view them through allows you to see more ‘moon’ at any one time.

Crafted in a supple seta leather, the Moonphase 37 comes with a luxurious blue Mastrotto strap. With its taper improved to 16mm (from 20mm), redesigned stainless steel Bader clasp it provides maximum comfort and is the perfect companion for both the 37 and 40mm case sizes.

The strap offering is also on point. There are size different coloured solid rubber straps to choose from, so you can match or contrast with your watch depending on your mood (there’s also a bracelet option if you prefer). And because each strap and bracelet is fitted with Christopher Ward’s quick-release system, you can swap in seconds.

The 26-jewel movement boasts a 4Hz frequency (equating to a smooth eight ticks per second) and a 38-hour power reserve. It also has an in-built anti-shock system to maintain accuracy when faced with any sudden jolts.

Own the summer with the new C60 Trident Reef dive watch. Four tropical colours inspired by endangered coral reefs. Six interchangeable rubber straps. And a multi-layered case construction that delivers comfort, lightness – and even more colour.

Available in 41mm and 44mm, the Reef’s stainless steel case boasts a four-piece, sandwich-style construction, allowing designers to bring contrasting shades together in the same case. It also provides water resistance to 200m.

Riffing on the ultra-legible Trident display, the Reef dial places an inner ring around the edge for extra contrast with one of the five ‘coral’ colours. Meanwhile, the outer dive bezel adds further colour – and the timing reassurance you need on deep dives.

The C60 Trident Reef has been created with Blue Marine Foundation, an ocean preservation charity sponsored by Christopher Ward. Not only is every colour reef-themed, but for each Reef sold, we’ll donate 2 percent of proceeds to Blue Marine as it fights overfishing around the world.

Love to change up your straps? Reef is for you. Each watch comes with a sturdy solid rubber strap, available in various coral colours. And thanks to our quick-release system you can swap between straps in seconds.
The Reef’s indexes and handset are deep-filled with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 GL C1, which provides an ultra-legible glow when lights are low.
When it comes to reliability and durability, the 26-jewel Sellita’s SW200-1 movement’s got your back. The 4hz frequency ensures a smooth sweep while the anti-shock system protects it from any knocks.

The Ti differs in other ways, too. The dial is here treated to a graduated tint, from dark charcoal at the edges to one of three exclusive colours at the centre. And inside lives a more sophisticated movement than the one in the standard steel model too. Sellita’s SW300-1 boasts chronometer certification and longer 56-hour power reserve, while its slimmer size allows for an even more wrist-hugging case. Indeed, it’s just 8.95mm tall, a full millimetre shorter than the steel version – just another remarkable stat about a remarkable watch.
This chronometer version has been tested by the Contrôle Officiel Suisse des Chronomètres, in a number of positions and temperatures to ensure precision timekeeping.

The Twelve’s bracelet is built from single links to deliver a taper that goes from 25mm to 17mm, while the satinised finish comes courtesy of a water-grinding process. The bracelet closes with a butterfly clasp – fitted with a micro-adjustment mechanism. This allows the wearer to adjust the length by up to 1.5mm per side – and 3mm in total.

sections.titleEn: We took our time, we thought differently, we built beautifully.
sections.bodyEn: Will Brackfield - designer

And, indeed, purples. The Ti dial boasts the same fascinating pyramid pattern as the regular Twelve, but in three new shades, each fading from dark charcoal at the circumference to bright colour at the centre.
This is one of those rare watches that’s almost as good-looking from the rear. In a playful tip of the hat to the Royal Oak, six large exposed screws hold down the 12-sided case back surround.
Even the hands and indices on the dial have been carefully reappraised, offering a riot of light-reflecting surfaces while using more understated and refined shapes than other Christopher Wards.

The luxury represented by The Twelve (Ti) requires every detail be given the utmost consideration, with transitions between surfaces particularly crucial. There are three finishes – sandblasting, polishing and linear brushing – on the bezel alone.
Why the man behind Patek Philippe’s Nautilus and the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak is horology’s greatest designer.
Six years in the making. Endless experimentation. A pause until our team knew they could achieve their ambitions. Enjoy the story of our first integrated watch in 13 years.

Turn the watch over and a sapphire crystal, placed in the 12-sided case back, displays the elaboré-finished rotor of the Sellita SW200-1 movement. Finally, take in the elegant, integrated Twelve bracelet, whose single-link design features a taper that goes from 25mm to 17mm and a butterfly clasp for easy removal.

The 26-jewel movement boasts a date wheel, a 4Hz frequency (equating to a smooth eight ticks per second) and a 38-hour power reserve. It also has an in-built anti-shock system to maintain accuracy when faced with any sudden jolts.
A new, polished, lacquered dial in Midnight Black, with elevated date window
Integrated bracelet with butterfly clasp for seamless removal
Lume-filled ‘Twelve’ indexes and handset

sections.titleEn: A field watch made for the skies
sections.bodyEn: Sellita SW200 COSC Befitting a watch named for the Royal Air Force, the C65 Cranwell is powered by extremely rugged and precise Swiss-made automatic movement - in this case, a chronometer-certified version of the Sellita SW200-1. Tested by the Controle Officiel Suisse des Chronometres, an institute responsible for ensuring the highest standards of horological excellence, the SW200-1 has been tested in a number of positions and temperatures to ensure precision timekeeping throughout.
“Each watch in the military collection sports some of the modern design touches from Christoper Ward.” – Thomas Calara
Licensed by the Ministry of Defence and approved by His Majesty’s Armed Forces, the second-gen C65 Cranwell is a precision-engineered update of Jaeger-LeCoultre and IWC’s ‘6B/346’ pilot’s watches.
The backplate has been deep-stamped with the Heraldic badge of the Royal Air Force – a reminder of the sacrifices its service men and women have made for us.
The completely redesigned dial now plays host to our two-flags logo, with oversized numerals that deliver instant legibility – a must for any military watch.
With brushed/polished surfaces and contoured lines, the 38mm Light-catcher™ case is an exercise in engineered elegance. Its subtle sizing makes it ideal for any wrist.

The large Arabic numerals are printed with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1, while Old Radium Super-LumiNova® is applied to the quarter-hour indexes (which you’ll also find on the inverted triangle at 12 o’clock).
Christopher Ward’s Military Collection gets its first upgrade since its launch in 2019 – with a set of stunning retro-style watches named after the Services’ world-famous training academies.

sections.titleEn: Inspired by the brave. Engineered by the best
sections.bodyEn: Take the ultra-tough, ultra-light forged carbon dial. Made from chopped carbon fibres infused with resin (there are around 500,000 fibres per square inch), forged carbon has a uniquely unfinished look, with the dark and light greys contrasting beautifully. Around the dial is a first for Christopher Ward: a rotating inner-compass bezel which lets you orientate yourself using the sun.

The movement boasts a 4Hz frequency (equating to a smooth eight ticks per second) and a 38-hour power reserve. It also has an in-built anti-shock system to maintain accuracy when faced with any sudden jolts.
The C60 Lympstone is the first Christopher Ward watch to carry an inner-compass bezel. You can orientate yourself by using it in conjunction with the sun.

The C60 Lympstone has the soul – and practicality – of a diving watch. Its outer bezel delivers a satisfying 120 clicks per circuit. So, when you mark your starting point with the pointer, you know it’ll stay in place.
The watch boasts a dial made of forged carbon – an ultra-tough, mouldable material made from chopped carbon fibres and resin. It gives the dial a marbled, near-camouflage look.

The C60 Lympstone indexes, hands and bezel are filled with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 GL C1, which delivers clarity in low light. Its potency is increased by exposing it to sunlight or artificial light, increasing the energy of its electrons.
Only when it had approved every part of the watch, did the Ministry of Defence allow the Marines’ official insignia to be laser-engraved into the caseback of the watch.

The marine-grade steel case has two crowns, one for rotating the compass, the other for winding the watch and moving the hands. Its gunmetal PVD coating ensures reflections – dangerous in combat – are kept to a minimum.

Sellita SW200-1 Automatic A workhorse watch demands a workhorse to power it, and you’ll find few hardier movements than Dune’s Sellita SW200-1 Automatic. It’s Swiss-made, self-winding, and known for accuracy, reliability and a useful 38-hour power reserve – so you can leave it on the bedside table for more than a day and it won’t need rewinding.

Dune’s fascinating sculpted three-dimensional wave pattern dial is ultra-legible whichever colour you pick: Eve (blue), Marram (green), Silica (grey) or Sand (white). Inspired by nature, they’re the sort of shades you might find on a 1950s Land Rover or ancient, sun-bleached hoodie. We’ve even dropped the date window, in the name of field watch purity.

Dune’s 38mm case is one of the most versatile around. Large enough to be easily read, yet small enough to neatly sidestep unwanted encounters with rocks and trees, it reflects the ‘wrist footprint’ of classic field watches. It looks and feels great on virtually any wrist.

Much of the Dune’s retro joy comes from its glass box crystal, a super-strong, bang-up-to-date version of the charismatic crystals you’d find on a 1970s sports watch; happily, it delivers the same charming retro ‘wobble’ when seen from the side.

That robust watches can be beautiful too is part of Dune’s raison d'être, which is why this is a rare field watch with an exhibition case back, allowing you to enjoy your Sellita movement with its elaboré-finished rotor any time you choose.

Dune lives for the outdoors, and when it’s dark out, lume matters. That’s why the handset and hour markers – right down to that cool ‘lollipop’ seconds hand – have been deep-filled with bright-glowing Super-LumiNova® BL Grade X. Even better, each dial colour gets its own specific, complementary shade of lume – a first for the range.

And this time, the dial does more than steal the show - it lights it. A brass base dial is coated with seven layers of custom Super-LumiNova®, creating a bed of light that charges quickly and shines intensely. Above floats a 1.4mm sapphire disc printed with Roman numerals, dual branding, and a minute track - both appearing to hover in mid-air during the day, and illuminated from below at night. The whole construction forms a miniature architectural light sculpture: playful, technical, and beautifully Studio Underd0g.

Missed out? The good news is the next opportunity starts with membership. Alliance members get first dibs on limited editions like the Alliance 02, plus priority access to British Watchmakers' Day, a year's free subscription to Oracle Time magazine, watch discounts and honestly, the most coveted enamel pin in British watchmaking.

Braided leather strap – a modern reinterpretation of the pocket-watch chain

With a daily routine that involves cleaning algae off endangered coral and swimming about a bit, the parrotfish doesn’t live the celebrity lifestyle.

But to Blue Marine it’s a superhero, keeping the tropical oceans’ ecosystem balanced and preventing algae from suffocating coral reefs. It also grinds up dead coral – and excretes it as white sand, helping to maintain beaches.

That’s why it’s the inspiration for the new Trident 30x30 : the first watch that directly promotes and supports their goal of having 30 percent of the oceans protected by 2030. Limited to 500 pieces, for every watch sold, we’ll give 2 percent of the price to Blue Marine, plus an extra £30 as a bonus.

The new wave-patterned dial is impossible to ignore, and mimics the ebb and flow of the tides. “This pattern is bespoke – and designed only for this watch,” says designer Matthew Sweatman.

The link to the parrotfish comes from the teal and red colour scheme, inspired by the #FishForTomorrow campaign by Blue Marine and The Maldives Resilient Reef. The project raised awareness of the link between coral reef health and that of the local fish population, one of which is the parrotfish.

In terms of visibility, the baton-shaped indices and handset are deep-filled with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1, which provides an ultra-legible glow when lights are low.

The watch uses a four-piece 41mm ‘sandwich’ case, first launched with last year’s Trident Reef, allowing designers to bring contrasting shades together in the same case. It also provides water resistance to 200m. Power comes from the 26-jewel Sellita SW200-2 Power + movement.

As a final nod to the work of Blue Marine, the Trident 30x30 is presented in a sleeve made from Notpla seaweed paper. Created from renewable seaweed and plant-based materials, Notpla is designed as a regenerative alternative to traditional packaging, helping to reduce waste while celebrating the potential of ocean-derived resources. The sleeve serves as a small but meaningful reflection of the project’s wider commitment to healthier oceans and a more sustainable future. Discover more about Notpla's seaweed-based materials here .

Sellita SW200-2 Power+ This improved incarnation of the Sellita SW200 movement delivers a generous power reserve of 65 hours. This is achieved through an optimised gear train, redesigned barrel and mainspring, enhanced automatic winding system, and updated balance assembly. This 26-jewel calibre is also more accurate than its predecessor, with an accuracy of -5/+12 seconds per day.

Finishing the movement is a new refined, skeletonised rotor: sandblasted beneath, with raised Christopher Ward text and a debossed twin-flags logo. Linear brushing across the upper surfaces contrasts with concentric circular brushing on the rotor weight – considered detailing, executed with precision.

Finishing the movement is a new refined, skeletonised rotor: sandblasted beneath, with raised Christopher Ward text and a debossed twin-flags logo. Linear brushing across the upper surfaces contrasts with concentric circular brushing on the rotor weight – considered detailing, executed with precision.

The new wave-pattern dial mimics the ebb and flow of the tides, whilst the red seconds hand complements the teal colour of the dial – all inspired by the colours of the parrotfish.
The new wave-pattern dial mimics the ebb and flow of the tides, whilst the red seconds hand complements the teal colour of the dial – all inspired by the colours of the parrotfish.
The countdown bezel adds further colour – and the timing reassurance you need on deep dives.
The applied twin flags logo and coral red ‘AUTOMATIC’ logotype add further depth and texture.
At 41mm, the matching, four-piece ‘sandwich’ case hits the sweet spot of presence and wearability.
Christopher Ward will give an extra £30 from sales to Blue Marine – on top of the existing 2 percent donation.
Presented in a Notpla seaweed-paper sleeve, combining innovative design with ocean-friendly materials.
The closed case back is deep-stamped with the 30x30 logo over a 3D wave pattern.

Somewhere in the Bay of Biscay, a storm is brewing. It's lent its name, and a little of its character, to the newest arrival in the Trident family.

Named after the stormy stretch of Atlantic Ocean between France and Spain, Biscay brings a refined, mid-century character to the Trident family.

Available in both 39mm and 42mm, the Biscay Automatic pairs Christopher Ward's Light-catcher™ case with a slim 11mm profile and a box sapphire crystal for an authentic vintage aesthetic.

"Though the case is similar to the Trident Pro's, it's slimmer and a different shape," says Christopher Ward designer Matthew Sweatman. "There's a smoother transition from polished to brushed surfaces."

And it's the surfaces that sing when you wear the Biscay Automatic, a constant light show that shimmers with every move of the wrist, day and night. The dial features minimal text, a granular texture and prominent Arabic numerals at 3, 6, 9 and 12 o'clock. Each is individually applied, providing depth and strong visual orientation.

The numerals are complemented by brushed and polished baton indexes and diamond-cut hands, all filled with a custom version Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL for a (non-radioactive) retro 'radium' look.

It also feels good in the hand. The aluminium bezel features a new, super-tough anodised surface, awash with lume for nocturnal visibility. Thanks to a more intricate tooth profile, it also has a better grip in-hand, so each of its 120 clicks feels precise and satisfying to turn. Water resistance is 200 metres, secured by a screw-down crown and case back.

Turn the Automatic over, and the exhibition case back provides a view into the SW300-1 automatic movement and its elaboré finishing and new rotor. It's available on either a hybrid strap, or Bader and Consort bracelets, both featuring Christopher Ward's new iLink™ tool-free resizing system.

Fair warning: once you've felt what Biscay's capable of, everything else feels like calm before the storm.

Sellita SW300-1 COSC COSC-certified chronometer The chronometer-certified SW300-1 is a true no-date version of Sellita’s SW300-1 automatic movement, whose calendar components are removed without any ‘phantom’ date position. Measuring just 3.6mm in height and 25.6mm in diameter, it beats at 28,800 vibrations per hour (4Hz) and uses 25 jewels to minimise friction and maximise durability. Displaying central hours, minutes, and sweeping seconds, it features hacking seconds and manual winding for accurate setting. A bidirectional winding rotor and optimised mainspring provide a power reserve of approximately 56 hours.

Bronze has weathered storms for centuries, from ships' bells to propellers, taking on the sea's abuse and wearing it well. This one's built for exactly that.

No two Biscay Bronzes will ever look the same. As the C60 Trident Biscay Bronze ages, its case develops a patina that's entirely its own, shaped by the air it's worn in, the wrist it sits on, and the life it lives along the way. Available in 39mm, it pairs Christopher Ward's redesigned Light-catcher™ case with a slim 11mm profile, a box sapphire crystal and the most sensual bezel action in watchmaking.

Rather than continuing with industry-standard 'CuSn6' bronze, Christopher Ward has adopted a marine-grade aluminium bronze alloy (the catchy 'CuAl10Ni5Fe4'), that's 10 percent aluminium, 5 percent nickel, 4 percent iron, and 100 percent gorgeous.

Used in the most demanding conditions at sea, the material offers greater resistance to seawater corrosion while retaining bronze's unique character. The result is a watch that develops its patina more gradually and evenly than traditional bronze, preserving its rich golden appearance for longer while still evolving over time.

As with the other Biscay Automatic, the Bronze features a box sapphire crystal, 200 metres of water resistance and the COSC-certified Sellita SW300-1 automatic movement. Rose-gold-plated hands add old-school luxury, while the signature Trident counterbalance and refined Light-catcher™ case ensure it remains unmistakably a Trident.

The dial features minimal text, a granular texture and prominent Arabic numerals at 3, 6, 9 and 12 o'clock, all individually applied. The numerals are complemented by brushed and polished baton indexes and diamond-cut hands, filled with a custom beige version of Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL for an aged, retro look.

The aluminium bezel features a new, super-tough anodised surface, awash with lume for nocturnal visibility. Thanks to a more intricate tooth profile, it also has a better grip in-hand, so each of its 120 clicks feels precise and satisfying to turn. Water resistance is 200 metres, secured by a screw-down crown and case back.

Turn the Biscay Bronze over, and the exhibition case back provides a view into the Sellita SW300-1 automatic movement and its elaboré finishing and new rotor. The watch is available on either a hybrid strap, or a distressed vintage oak leather strap, both featuring Christopher Ward's quick-release system for easy changing.

Fair warning: once you've felt what Biscay's capable of, everything else feels like calm before the storm.

Sellita SW300-1 COSC COSC-certified chronometer The chronometer-certified SW300-1 is a true no-date version of Sellita’s SW300-1 automatic movement, whose calendar components are removed without any ‘phantom’ date position. Measuring just 3.6mm in height and 25.6mm in diameter, it beats at 28,800 vibrations per hour (4Hz) and uses 25 jewels to minimise friction and maximise durability. Displaying central hours, minutes, and sweeping seconds, it features hacking seconds and manual winding for accurate setting. A bidirectional winding rotor and optimised mainspring provide a power reserve of approximately 56 hours.

Named after the North Atlantic's most treacherous coastline, the new C60 Trident Biscay GMT takes a bearing on trouble and doesn't flinch.

Available in both 39mm and 42mm, the GMT builds on the design of the automatic Biscay, introducing a dedicated fourth hand for tracking an additional time zone, alongside a bidirectional aluminium bezel in a two-tone colour combination, to mark day from night. And thanks to its redesigned Light-catcher™ case, it adds 200m water resistance for good measure.

As with every Biscay, the new bezel is surface-hardened. It reaches 250HV on the micro-Vickers hardness scale, the industry-standard measure of how well a metal resists surface wear, making it 67 percent harder than untreated aluminium and helping to preserve the crisp finish over time. A more defined tooth profile gives the bi-directional bezel a better grip in-hand, so each of its 120 clicks feels precise and satisfying to turn.

The balanced dial layout replaces the 6 o'clock Arabic numeral with a date aperture, maintaining harmony while adding practicality. The numerals are complemented by brushed and polished baton indexes and diamond-cut hands, all filled with a custom-made Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL for a retro 'radium' look.

"With the Trident Pro 300 GMT bezel, only the large triangle at 12 is made of luminous material," says CW product director Jörg Bader. "But with Biscay's bezel we've used it everywhere: on the numbers, the dots, the lot. Short of a Lumière, nothing out-glows Biscay."

Inside, sits the COSC-certified Sellita SW330-2 automatic movement, delivering up to 56 hours of power reserve alongside dependable 'caller' GMT functionality. Turn the watch over, and the exhibition case back provides a view into the Sellita movement, and its Colimaçoné finishing and new rotor. The watch is available on Hybrid and Cordura straps, or a Bader or Consort bracelet, both featuring Christopher Ward's new iLink™ tool-free resizing system.

Fair warning: once you've seen what Biscay's capable of, everything else feels like calm before the storm.

Sellita SW330-2 GMT COSC-certified chronometer The Sellita SW330-2 is a Swiss-made automatic GMT calibre based on the architecture of the SW300 family. Measuring 25.6mm in diameter and 4.1mm in height, it operates at a frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour (4Hz) and incorporates 25 jewels. The movement features central hours, minutes, seconds, a date display – and an independently adjustable 24-hour GMT hand for tracking a second time zone. Automatic winding is delivered via a bidirectional rotor system, while the improved mainspring provides a power reserve of around 56 hours.
